default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-978.title: Regression-slope t-stat follow
E-978.hypothesis: A statistically significant linear drift of the day's return over a window means a persistent flow is working an order; the first bar where the slope t-stat exceeds the threshold is early in that flow.

E-979.title: Opening-range midpoint cross follow
E-979.hypothesis: After the opening range is formed its midpoint is the balance point; a close that moves clear of it to one side shows the opening auction resolving that way.

E-980.title: Typical-path deviation fade
E-980.hypothesis: Intraday flow has a recurring time-of-day shape (average return path from the open over recent sessions); a stretch far from that path is a one-off imbalance that tends to mean-revert toward it.

E-981.title: V-shape completion follow
E-981.hypothesis: When price drops (or spikes) by an unusual amount and then recovers to the level where the move began, the sellers/buyers who pushed it are trapped and the recovery continues.

E-982.title: Realized semivariance dominance follow
E-982.hypothesis: When squared up-moves dominate squared down-moves over a window, buyers are the ones moving price in jumps; the asymmetry of realized variance is a persistent-pressure marker.

E-983.title: US-open window drift follow
E-983.hypothesis: The US cash open (10:30 or 11:30 Sao Paulo depending on DST) brings foreign flow into the index; the direction of the first minutes after it tends to carry.

E-984.title: Multi-session mean-price cross follow
E-984.hypothesis: The average price of the last several sessions is the multi-day fair value that swing holders anchor on; a close through it shifts inventory control for the day.

E-985.title: Previous-block midpoint cross follow
E-985.hypothesis: The midpoint of the previous clock block's range is where the last block balanced; clearing it by a fraction of that range signals the new block's direction.

E-986.title: Level-stack alignment onset
E-986.hypothesis: When price holds above (or below) the day open, the session VWAP and the previous close together, every reference group of participants is on one side, so no one is defending against the move.

E-987.title: Prior last-hour band re-entry
E-987.hypothesis: The previous session's last hour is where its final inventory was set; price coming back into that band from outside is the market accepting the old closing value and tends to keep going through it.
